Snapdragon X2 Elite standard 18-core Signal65 report October 2026

content.text:
Snapdragon X2 Elite Performance: Signal65 compares three retail 14-inch systems: Lenovo Slim 7x with standard 18-core Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-88-100, Dell XPS 14 with Intel Core Ultra X7 358H, and Lenovo Yoga 7a 14 with AMD Ryzen AI 7 445. It reports Snapdragon leads over the Intel system of 31% in Geekbench 7 multicore and 24% single-core, and 97% versus Intel's 95% average performance retention across six battery benchmarks. The report also records Intel wins in integrated graphics and sustained Office battery runtime. It describes whole-system comparisons and flags configuration differences; Windows Central identifies Qualcomm as the study commissioner. (time=2026-10-01; cutoff=UNKNOWN).
Qualcomm's “non-Extreme” Snapdragon X2 just embarrassed Intel's premium laptop strategy: Rubino reports the standard-chip comparison and its CPU, AI, productivity, and battery results. The article says Qualcomm commissioned the study; notes Intel's roughly 23% lead in the cited graphics test and its 17.4-hour versus 14.3-hour sustained Office battery result; and discusses the $750 tested-system price gap and display differences as context for whole-laptop and battery comparisons. (time=2026-10-01T18:38:23Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme Performance: Signal65's research listing dates this earlier Extreme-tier comparison August 13, 2026. Used only to establish the prior flagship-comparison context, not for its benchmark findings. (time=2026-08-13; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
